_doc: One proposed disposition per skill in plugins/*/skills. Every entry is PROPOSED: Andy decides the batch, and nothing here has been merged or deleted. A merge or retire names where the job goes (mergeInto or coveredBy), because frequency alone never decides. Drills are emergency or rare-by-design skills and stay retained whatever their frequency. Checked by tooling/test-skill-dispositions.js. Each wired hook also names why it exists (hooks[].because): kind model is a model weakness with a retest to run after a model bump, kind harness is a Claude Code or OS gap. retested names the model those reasons were last checked against. A retest proposes, it never retires.

hooks.because: A new or compacted session starts blind to sprint state, plugin drift, dirty tree, parallel work and its own handoff file.
The agent-browser binary leaves a zombie Chromium on Windows that blanks Chrome and steals Win+Shift+S, and it registers itself to start at boot.
The peer session registry is kept per CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so sessions under another account are invisible and their liveness is unknown.
Nothing in Claude Code warns when the always-on rule set grows over budget, loses a required rule, or carries conflicting style directives.
The harness never truncates SessionStart env files, so repeated plugin exports push the Bash command prefix past the Windows length cap.
Given a screenshot, the model answers only what the user asked about and misses other visible defects in the image.
hooks.retest: Show 20 screenshots with planted secondary defects, hook off, and count the defects reported unasked.

hooks.because: Claude cannot see files the user drops into the inbox folder, so screenshots sent for a prompt go unnoticed unless something announces them.
The model edits the installed plugin tree, hook and lint configs, or writes private names into public repos, and wastes tokens reading generated files.
hooks.retest: Log protected-path writes, private-name writes and generated-file reads over 20 sessions with the hook logging only.

hooks.because: The model sends option panels with no Recommended mark, and keeps asking the absent operator questions while AWAY is active.
hooks.retest: With the hook off, count unmarked panels and AWAY-time questions per 100 panels across 20 sessions.

hooks.because: Coordinators send many messages to one session in an hour even with the batching rule in context, and the cost lands on the receiver's context.
hooks.retest: Count recipients that get more than 3 messages in an hour during an overnight Brain run with the hook off.

hooks.because: A coordinator with no worker to start works product repos itself, and sessions bypass hooks with --no-verify or merge PRs past merge-lock.
hooks.retest: Replay Brain runs with the hook in log mode and count commit, push, merge or rebase outside home repos.

hooks.because: Headless workers background a long command such as the gate, end their turn, and report it passed while it is still running.
hooks.retest: Run 20 headless workers with the hook logging only and count backgrounded commands and premature pass claims.

hooks.because: The model runs a package install in a worktree whose node_modules is hardlinked to main, which rewrites the main checkout's packages too.
hooks.retest: Count installs attempted inside shared-install worktrees over 20 worker runs with the hook in log mode.

hooks.because: Sessions write shared artifact rows with field names, enum values or future timestamps the page cannot use, and the tool accepts them without complaint.
hooks.retest: Log schema violations in ArtifactData writes over 20 sessions with the hook set to log only.

hooks.because: A queued peer message is lost when the receiver stops before processing it, and the host keeps no record that joins sender and receiver.
The model edits TypeScript and ends its turn without typechecking, so this records the edited files for the Stop-time check.
hooks.retest: With both typecheck hooks off, count responses ending with type or lint errors across 20 edit-heavy sessions.

hooks.because: Claude Code keeps no local per-tool-call record of sizes and failures to measure behaviour from later.
The model ends a turn while prd.json or the mission queue still has pending work, so an unattended sprint stalls without anyone noticing.
hooks.retest: Count turns that end with pending stories in 20 auto runs with the hook off.

hooks.because: Spawned sessions that finish work go quiet instead of reporting to the coordinator, even when the brief asks them to report.
hooks.retest: In an overnight fleet run with the hook off, count sessions that committed work and never messaged the Brain.

hooks.because: The model does not track its own context depth, so it neither saves a handoff before auto-compaction lands nor sheds expensive context.
hooks.retest: With the hook off, count compactions past 250k that land with no fresh handoff, over 20 long sessions.

hooks.because: After a quota reset the model forgets that workflow agents lost at the wall can be resumed, and starts the run over from scratch.
hooks.retest: After 10 quota-wall losses with the hook off, count sessions that resume via resumeFromRunId unprompted.

hooks.because: The model ends a response that left type or lint errors in the files it edited, and claims done without running the check.
hooks.retest: With the hook off, count responses whose edited files fail typecheck or lint across 20 sessions.

hooks.because: Sessions do not keep their fleet intent record current, so after an outage the coordinator cannot tell what each one was doing.
hooks.retest: With the hook off, measure how often intent records are missing or behind the branch head after 20 fleet sessions.

hooks.because: A turn killed by an API error skips the Stop hooks, so a stalled sprint leaves no record and looks mid-run to the next session.
Compaction can lose sprint state mid-run, so prd.json is copied to a snapshot first in case it needs recovering.
Compaction drops the model's working state, so the session needs pointing back at the saved prd.json snapshot to resume the right story.
A rule file that never reaches context fails silently, and the harness gives no record of which instruction files actually loaded.
A new session starts with no knowledge of earlier sessions in the project, so this opens a memory session and injects their carried-over notes.
Claude Code keeps no memory across sessions, so tool calls are captured as observations and a brief is shown the first time an area is touched.
Nothing persists what a session achieved once it ends, so this closes the memory session with a summary a later session can read.
